<description>
`BerkeleyRODatabase::Open` reads an overflow record by following `next_page` until it is 0. #34959 added a check that stops once more data than `item_len` was read, which needs every page to add data. An overflow page with `hf_offset` 0 adds none. If such a page names itself as `next_page`, the loop reads it again and again and never ends.

This PR treats an overflow page without data as corruption.

**Behavior change:** a file with an empty overflow page no longer opens and fails with `Overflow page has no data`. Before, an empty page with `next_page` 0 was accepted and the record came out shorter than `item_len`.

**Measurement:** regtest, RelWithDebInfo, base a527a0077a. The file has 5 pages of 4096 bytes: one key whose value is an overflow record with `item_len` 100, and one overflow page.

| overflow page | master | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hf_offset` 0, `next_page` itself | `bitcoin-wallet dump` at 100 % of one core, killed after 60 s | fails at once, exit 1 |
| `hf_offset` 100, `next_page` 0 | dumped in 0.11 s | dumped as before |

With `migratewallet` on master the RPC does not return and one HTTP worker stays at 100 % CPU. Other RPCs still answer, but `stop` had not finished after 30 s.

**Tests:** new case in `tool_wallet.py` that writes both files by hand. On master it hangs (killed after 90 s). Passing locally: `test_bitcoin` and `test_runner.py` with the default list. Not run: fuzz targets, lint.

Contributed by [turingpoint](https://www.turingpoint.de).
</description>

<commits>
d5878da5ac wallet, bdbro: Reject overflow pages without data

An overflow record is read by following next_page until it is 0. The
length check added in dc3a2b9c3b6 stops the loop once more data than
item_len was read, which needs every page to add data. An overflow
page with hf_offset 0 adds nothing, so a page like that which names
itself as next_page is read again and again. bitcoin-wallet dump and
migratewallet then spin on one core and never return.

BDB does not write overflow pages without data, so treat one as
corruption.

Signed-off-by: Jan Kahmen <jan@turingpoint.de>

e2f3e91d95 test: Check that bdbro rejects an empty overflow page

Write a small BDB file by hand whose only overflow page has no data
and links to itself, and check that bitcoin-wallet dump fails instead
of looping. A second file with a filled overflow page is dumped as
before.

Signed-off-by: Jan Kahmen <jan@turingpoint.de>
</commits>

diff --git a/src/wallet/migrate.cpp b/src/wallet/migrate.cpp
index 6e5f8a493b..ce6085f7dc 100644
--- a/src/wallet/migrate.cpp
+++ b/src/wallet/migrate.cpp
@@ -699,6 +699,11 @@ void BerkeleyRODatabase::Open()
                         }
                         OverflowPage opage(opage_header);
                         db_file >> opage;
+                        if (opage.data.empty()) {
+                            // A page that adds nothing makes no progress towards item_len,
+                            // so a chain of such pages could link back to itself forever

+                        }

                             throw std::runtime_error("Overflow record data is larger than stated size");
diff --git a/test/functional/tool_wallet.py b/test/functional/tool_wallet.py
index 41ef14a526..41123b7cbd 100755
--- a/test/functional/tool_wallet.py
+++ b/test/functional/tool_wallet.py
@@ -6,6 +6,7 @@
 
 import os
 import stat
+import struct
 import subprocess
 import textwrap
 
@@ -434,6 +435,65 @@ class ToolWalletTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
         else:
             assert False, "Big transaction was not found in wallet dump"
 
+    def test_dump_bdb_empty_overflow_page(self):
+        self.log.info("Test that a BDB file with an empty overflow page that links to itself is rejected")
+
+        # Minimal BDB btree file with 5 pages: outer metadata, outer root, inner metadata,
+        # a leaf with one key whose value is an overflow record, and the overflow page.
+        page_size = 4096
+
+        def page_header(page_num, next_page, entries, hf_offset, level, page_type):
+            return struct.pack("<IIIIIHHBB", 0, 1, page_num, 0, next_page, entries, hf_offset, level, page_type)
+
+        def meta_page(page_num, root):
+            page = struct.pack("<IIIIII", 0, 1, page_num, 0x00053162, 9, page_size)
+            page += struct.pack("<BBBB", 0, 9, 0, 0)  # BTREE_META
+            page += struct.pack("<IIIII", 0, 4, 0, 0, 0)  # last_page is 4
+            page += struct.pack("<I", 0x20)  # SUBDB
+            page += bytes(20)
+            page += struct.pack("<IIIII", 0, 2, 0, 0, root)
+            return page.ljust(page_size, b"\x00")
+
+        def leaf_page(page_num, records):
+            page = bytearray(page_size)
+            offset = page_size
+            indexes = b""
+            for record in records:
+                offset -= len(record)
+                page[offset:offset + len(record)] = record
+                indexes += struct.pack("<H", offset)
+            header = page_header(page_num, 0, len(records), offset, 1, 5) + indexes
+            page[:len(header)] = header
+            return bytes(page)
+
+        def data_record(data):
+            return struct.pack("<HB", len(data), 1) + data
+
+        def overflow_record(page_num, item_len):
+            return struct.pack("<HBBII", 0, 3, 0, page_num, item_len)
+
+        def write_wallet(name, overflow_page):
+            wallet_dir = self.nodes[0].wallets_path / name
+            wallet_dir.mkdir()
+            with open(wallet_dir / self.wallet_data_filename, "wb") as f:
+                f.write(meta_page(0, 1))
+                f.write(leaf_page(1, [data_record(b"main"), data_record(struct.pack(">I", 2))]))
+                f.write(meta_page(2, 3))
+                f.write(leaf_page(3, [data_record(b"\x04name"), overflow_record(4, 100)]))
+                f.write(overflow_page.ljust(page_size, b"\x00"))
+
+        # An overflow page that holds the whole item can be dumped
+        write_wallet("bdb_overflow", page_header(4, 0, 0, 100, 0, 7) + b"A" * 100)
+        wallet_dump = self.nodes[0].datadir_path / "bdb_overflow.dump"
+        self.assert_tool_output("The dumpfile may contain private keys. To ensure the safety of your Bitcoin, do not share the dumpfile.\n", "-wallet=bdb_overflow", f"-dumpfile={wallet_dump}", "dump")
+        assert_equal(self.read_dump(wallet_dump)["046e616d65"], (b"A" * 100).hex())
+
+        # An overflow page without data that names itself as the next page
+        write_wallet("bdb_empty_overflow", page_header(4, 4, 0, 0, 0, 7))
+        wallet_dump = self.nodes[0].datadir_path / "bdb_empty_overflow.dump"
+        self.assert_raises_tool_error("Overflow page has no data", "-wallet=bdb_empty_overflow", f"-dumpfile={wallet_dump}", "dump")
+        assert not wallet_dump.exists()
+
     def test_no_create_legacy(self):
         self.log.info("Test that legacy wallets cannot be created")
 
@@ -463,6 +523,7 @@ class ToolWalletTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
         self.test_dump_createfromdump()
         self.test_chainless_conflicts()
         self.test_dump_very_large_records()
+        self.test_dump_bdb_empty_overflow_page()
         self.test_no_create_legacy()
         self.test_no_create_unnamed()
